historical_growth.owner_fcf_series_note: Owner FCF (reported FCF less SBC), FY2016-FY2025: 376, 809, 1,489, 1,309, 4,011, 2,333, 3,024, 4,919, 2,055, -135. CAGRs ending FY2025 are undefined (negative end value); the series is dominated by land-inventory swings (FY2020 and FY2023 are land run-offs, FY2025-26 a spec-home build), so no FCF CAGR is a usable growth anchor. Cumulative FY2019-FY2025 OCF 19.3bn against 23.5bn net income (~82% conversion through a full cycle including the Millrose land distribution).
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: base-path 10-year average (long-run US household formation plus nominal pricing). Equity CAGRs are not usable: the Feb-2025 Millrose spin-off distributed ~5.5bn of book value and ~8bn of buybacks since FY2021 shrink equity independently of returns; revenue CAGRs are distorted by the FY2018 CalAtlantic merger (10yr) and the FY2021-22 price peak (3yr/5yr).
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 4.1% vs revenue 5yr 8.7% and EPS 5yr 0.3% -- divergence >30% in both directions, caused by the Millrose distribution and buybacks (equity) and by the FY2022 margin peak unwinding (EPS). None of the three is used as the forward anchor.

scenario_narratives.base: Lennar's axes are (1) the mortgage-rate path and what it does to affordability-driven incentives, which at ~12% of ASP are the whole gap between today's 15.8% gross margin and a normal 20-22%; (2) the land-light trade -- lower, steadier margins and far lower capital, with Millrose and other land bankers paid through cost of sales; (3) the volume-first strategy, which protects cost per square foot and cycle time but sets price. Base: FY2027 is a third weak year -- rates stay near 7%, the backlog and order ASP reset revenue down ~2% and margin barely lifts off the trough -- then rates ease and the structural shortage (household formation against a decade of under-building) lifts volume 4-5% a year. Margin recovers to a 10% land-light mid-cycle by FY2032 and holds; the terminal multiple is ~12.8x owner FCF, a cyclical's multiple, not a compounder's.
scenario_narratives.bull: Rate relief arrives in 2027. Incentives fall to ~5%, gross margin returns to 20%+ and SG&A re-levers below 8% as Lennar grows deliveries 6-7% for three years on the same community count; EBITDA margin reaches 12%, the FY2019-FY2020 structure, on a larger and less capital-intensive base. Buybacks continue at ~1.5-2bn a year from positive owner FCF.
scenario_narratives.bear: Inflation keeps the 30-year rate at 7-7.5% through 2027-28 (the October 2026 CPI print and Fannie Mae's raised 2027 forecast point this way) and consumer confidence keeps sliding (the Q3 release says conditions 'deteriorated since our last earnings call'). Lennar holds volume by cutting price another 8%, incentives rise further, margin troughs near 5.5% and inventory of completed homes needs discounting. Recovery is slow and stalls at 8% EBITDA because option premiums are a permanent cost and the asset-light structure caps margin. The balance sheet survives comfortably (net homebuilding debt to capital 12.7%), so the bear is an earnings trough, not solvency.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the land-light homebuilder on mid-cycle owner FCF, not on the FY2026 trough and not on the FY2021-22 peak. The trough is explicit in FY0 (6.3% EBITDA, trailing owner FCF of 2% of revenue after a spec-home inventory build) and each scenario is a different recovery path, so cyclicality is priced once, in the flows, with a single 10.5% WACC and a 13x terminal cap. Segments whose earnings are noise (Multifamily, LENx marks) are excluded from the flows and carried at book in the bridge; the mortgage warehouse is excluded from debt with its matching loans. This update does three things: corrects the discount rate to a 5.1% 10-year, pushes the base recovery out a year, and shifts five points of weight from bull to bear -- the 2027 outlook has darkened since September while the filed numbers have not changed. The number to act on is the probability-weighted value; the 15% hurdle entry price is what a buyer should pay to be compensated for a cyclical whose next two years are the uncertain ones. Q4 FY2026 results in mid-December will supersede the guided FY0.
key_risks_to_valuation: Mortgage rates: every 1pp on the 30-year moves affordability-driven incentives by several points of gross margin; the bear case is a rate path, not a company-specific failure.
Mid-cycle margin assumption (10% EBITDA): the land-light model has no full-cycle history. If option-premium land cost plus volume-first pricing cap EBITDA nearer 8%, the base value is ~bear.

Working-capital assumption (-25% capture): the engine releases cash when revenue falls, but Lennar's volume-first strategy has done the opposite -- 9M FY2026 OCF was -822 against +827 net earnings as inventories rose 1,739 and deposits 795 on revenue down 8%. If that persists through FY2027, year-1 and year-2 owner FCF are overstated by roughly 0.5-1.0bn each (~$2-4/share per year).

Terminal multiple and discount rate: ~12.8x owner FCF (Gordon at 10.5%/2.5%, just inside the 13x cap) is above where homebuilders trade at cyclical peaks. Each 0.5pp of WACC is worth ~$4.40/share of weighted value; the 10-year has ranged 4.4-5.3% in six months.
Lennar Other / Multifamily carried at book (1.34bn net, ~$5.6/share): LENx public stakes are marked to market and have lost 62 in nine months; a further halving removes ~$1.50/share.
Share count: continued ~1-2bn/yr buybacks below intrinsic value are value-accretive and NOT in the model (flat count); conversely, buying back at the 2025 average of $113 was not.
FY0 is still a guided number: Q4 FY2026 (22,000-23,000 deliveries, 15.5-16% gross margin, $370-380k ASP) reports mid-December 2026; guidance has been cut after each quarter this year.

Net homebuilding debt was only 643.4 at 30-Nov-2025; the 2.5bn swing in nine months is 1,850 of finished-home/WIP inventory build, 737+256 of buybacks and 370 of dividends against 827 of net earnings.

Nine-month FY2026 OCF is -822 against +827 of net earnings: inventories +1,739 and option deposits +795 absorbed it, and Q3 alone was still -104. Q4 is the seasonal cash quarter (Q4 FY2025 OCF +1,759), so the TTM figure rests on one strong quarter. The projection does not carry the inventory build forward, which is why year-1 owner FCF (1,428, 4.6% of revenue) sits well above the trailing 2.1% -- see key_risks.

No separate equity-award tax-withholding line is disclosed and Lennar's awards are restricted stock without a net-settlement cash figure, so the add-back is used alone. Stated on the same TTM window as reported_fcf so that last_fcf = reported_fcf - sbc ties (the prior build carried the FY2025 figure here against a TTM last_fcf).

inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate build. Risk-free 5.07% (10y UST, ^TNX close 2026-11-18; it has held 4.9-5.3% since mid-September), ERP 5.0%, homebuilder beta ~1.35 -> cost of equity ~11.8%; pre-tax cost of debt ~6.2% on the senior notes/revolver, ~4.6% after tax; weights ~82% equity (237.9m x price ~19.7bn) / 18% debt (4.3bn) -> 10.5%. CORRECTION to the 2026-10-02 build, which used a 4.3% risk-free and 10.0%: the 10-year was already ~5.2% that week, so the prior rate was stale rather than the market having moved since. Same WACC in all three scenarios: cyclicality is charged in the flows via scenario paths and weights, not a second time in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP ASC 842: office and equipment operating leases are expensed within SG&A and already inside OCF; lease liabilities are immaterial relative to a 4.3bn debt stack and are excluded from net debt. No separate lease charge (lease_cost_pct_path omitted).
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the bridge: noncontrolling interests of 137.5 (31-Aug-2026) deducted. Flows are built on consolidated revenue, but NCI took only 8.9 of 827.0 nine-month net earnings (~1%), so consolidated and attributable flows are within rounding.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (operating company, cyclical -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md), mid-cycle normalisation of a trough year. Lennar is the largest-volume US homebuilder, land-light since the Feb-2025 Millrose Properties spin-off (owns <2.5% of its ~488,000 controlled homesites; land flows through option deposits of 7.3bn and option premiums in cost of sales). The engine's EBITDA is consolidated: homebuilding gross margin less SG&A, plus Financial Services operating earnings (mortgage/title for Lennar's own buyers -- an operating segment, already net of warehouse interest), less corporate G&A and the charitable contribution, before capitalised-interest-in-COGS and D&A. FY2026E EBITDA ~1,970 / 6.3% (9M EBIT 1,250 + D&A ~102, plus a guided Q4 at ~7%) is a trough: incentives are ~12% of ASP against a normal ~5-6%, gross margin 15.8% against 20-23% in FY2019-FY2024 and 27.5% at the FY2022 peak. Peak is NOT the anchor. Pre-COVID (FY2015-FY2019) consolidated EBITDA margins ran ~10-12% with owned land; the land-light model trades ~1-2pp of margin for lower capital intensity, so mid-cycle is taken as ~10% (base), 12% (bull: pre-COVID structure restored through scale and the 14% construction-cost reduction since Q4-2023), 8% (bear: incentives stay elevated through a long affordability recession). Multifamily and Lennar Other (LENx technology stakes marked to market, -62 in 9M FY2026) are OUTSIDE the flows and enter the bridge at book net assets. Working capital: inventory-heavy, so capture is NEGATIVE (-25% of the revenue change; owned inventory 11.5bn + deposits 7.3bn less payables 1.8bn is ~55% of revenue, but the land-light model finances most of the growth through option deposits, so a quarter of each incremental dollar is modelled as consumed). Cash tax 25.5% (FY2026 Q3 ETR 26.4%, including state tax and non-deductible compensation; Lennar is a full cash taxpayer -- FY2025 cash taxes 988.5). Terminal cap 13x owner FCF for a cyclical (at the 10.5% WACC the Gordon multiple at g=2.5% is 12.8x, so Gordon now binds marginally below the cap in every scenario). Q4 FY2026 results (mid-December 2026) replace FY0 with an actual and bring FY2027 guidance; that is the evidence that would move base_revenue, the year-1 drivers and wc_capture. Berkshire Hathaway's ~11-12% stake is noted but is not a valuation input.

bear.rationale: A two-year affordability recession: mortgage rates stay near 7%, Lennar keeps its volume-first strategy by cutting price (revenue -8% then -4%), incentives rise above 13% and margin falls to ~5.5% before a slow recovery that stalls at 8% because the land-light option-premium cost is permanent and competitors match on price. Not a 2008-style balance-sheet event -- owned land is <2.5% of homesites, so losses would hit 7.3bn of option deposits rather than a land book -- but a long, flat earnings trough. Path UNCHANGED from 2026-10-02; its rate premise is now close to the published 2027 forecasts, which is why its weight rises to 30%.

base.rationale: FY2027 is a third soft year, not the first year of recovery: Q3 orders -9% in units at a $359k order ASP against $372k delivered, backlog dollars -5%, and the late-2026 forecasts in Analysis.json (Fannie Mae's 2027 mortgage-rate view lifted to ~7.5%, NAHB sentiment at 2012 levels) remove the rate relief the prior path leaned on. Revenue -2% (volume held near 81-82k on 3% more communities, ASP down ~3%), +3% in FY2028, then 4-5% as the structural shortage reasserts, fading to 2.5%. EBITDA margin lifts only 0.3pp off the 6.3% FY2026 trough in FY2027 (incentives have eased 14.1% -> 12.0% of ASP through FY2026 and Q4 gross margin is guided flat at 15.5-16%), then ~0.7-0.8pp a year to the 10% land-light mid-cycle in FY2032 -- one year later than the 2026-10-02 path. It never revisits the FY2021-22 peak (18%+). CHANGED vs prior: growth years 1-2 (-1.0/4.0 -> -2.0/3.0) and margin years 1-5 (7.0/7.8/8.6/9.3/10.0 -> 6.6/7.3/8.1/8.9/9.6). Everything else unchanged.

bull.rationale: Rates fall through 2027, the even-flow machine (4.1 starts/community/month, 116-day cycle time, construction cost -14% since Q4-2023) converts into volume growth of 6-7% for three years, incentives drop toward 5% and the pre-COVID 12% EBITDA structure is restored on a larger base despite the land-light margin give-up. Path UNCHANGED from 2026-10-02; the darker 2027 consensus is reflected in the bull weight (25% -> 20%), not by redrawing the tail.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 13x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from 25/50/25 (2026-10-02) to 30/50/20; house default is 15/50/35. Bear 30%: its premise -- mortgage rates stuck at 7%+ through 2027-28 -- has gone from a tail to roughly the published forecast (Fannie Mae ~7.5% for 2027, NAHB calling a third weak year), though the bear also needs price cuts of 8% then 4% and a permanently capped 8% margin, which the easing incentive trend (14.1% -> 12.0% of ASP in FY2026) argues against; hence 30%, not 40%. Base 50%: a delayed recovery to a 10% mid-cycle. Bull 20%: it needs rate relief arriving in 2027 AND incentives normalising without volume loss, and the first leg is now against consensus. Balance-sheet risk stays low (12.7% net homebuilding debt to capital, owned land <2.5% of homesites), which keeps the bear an earnings trough rather than a solvency case. Berkshire Hathaway building an 11-12% stake is not treated as evidence on the flows and moves no weight.
